hypotheses.title: Amplitude-invariant, cross-physics phase-congruency edges
layers: Cached GeoDAWN total magnetic intensity (tmi; input band 14)
Cached isostatic gravity anomaly (iso_grav_anom; input band 13)
Optional separate basement-depth corroboration (depth_to_base_surf; input band 15)
hypotheses.physical_signature: At several frozen spatial scales, compute local phase congruency from quadrature/log-Gabor responses, estimate edge normals, and reward co-located magnetic and gravity phase-aligned edges. Basement-depth edge agreement may be a capped corroborator, not a learned label-derived feature.
hypotheses.why_it_may_find_catalogue_missing_faults: A buried fault can juxtapose susceptibility, density, or basement depth under alluvial cover while producing a weak-amplitude boundary and little preserved surface scarp. Local phase alignment is intended to retain coherent boundaries across wavelength scales when absolute anomaly amplitude varies. It is a fault-favorability hypothesis, not direct evidence of a fault or geothermal vent.
hypotheses.difference_from_repository_prior_art: The exact multiscale phase-congruency transform was not found in tracked implementation code. H33-6 tested aligned raw gradient edges, while other work used Hessian/ridge transforms, scarp line integrals, dip projection, and catalogue-supervised fusion. This proposal changes the signal representation to local phase congruency; it still shares geophysical layers with prior art and therefore has material duplicate risk.
hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Intrusive or stratigraphic contacts, magnetic-domain boundaries, GeoDAWN survey seams, and gridding/processing artifacts can create aligned magnetic-gravity edges without a fault.
hypotheses.qualitative_expected_improvement: Rank 1 of this slate; moderate-to-high plausibility relative to the cached-stack candidates, but unmeasured and not a numeric DTI estimate.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium-high: multiscale oriented filtering over a 5-million-cell footprint, feature-alone canary, and memory/runtime benchmarking; use the shared cache/evaluator rather than a private stack.

hypotheses.title: Scale-persistent basement/gravity ridge bifurcation graph
layers: Cached depth_to_base_surf and its scale-space ridge/curvature channels
Optional ext_TMI_up150 as a third, capped physical corroborator
hypotheses.physical_signature: Extract ridges independently at frozen smoothing scales, track ridge branches across scale, and score persistent Y-junctions or branch terminations only when a second potential-field layer supports the local edge orientation. The graph is constructed from subsurface fields, not catalogue traces or vent seeds.
hypotheses.why_it_may_find_catalogue_missing_faults: Concealed basement steps and relay-zone splays can produce branching density or basement-depth boundaries without a mapped surface trace. Requiring persistence across scale aims to reject one-pixel noise and unstable interpolation features.
hypotheses.difference_from_repository_prior_art: No exact scale-persistent Y-junction statistic for the basement/gravity fields was found in tracked implementation code. Existing work includes fault-tip/stepover geometry, ridge persistence, line networks, and least-cost connectivity; this candidate is conceptually adjacent to those methods, so novelty is uncertain and must be screened before placement.
hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Intersecting lithologic contacts, basin margins, magnetic basement domains, and interpolation seams may form persistent ridge junctions without displacement.
hypotheses.qualitative_expected_improvement: Rank 2; plausible but lower confidence than H27-PHASEEDGE because persistent junctions may be common in non-fault geology and the repository already contains related ridge/network methods.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium: multiscale skeleton/graph extraction plus matched controls, feature-alone canaries, and an early continuous-surface uniqueness stop.

hypotheses.title: Repeated cross-valley profile asymmetry and channel deflection
layers: Raw USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation tiles (required for the intended trace-scale test)
Cached det_elev, depth_to_base_surf, and gravity fields for regional structural context
hypotheses.physical_signature: Measure signed cross-valley elevation-profile asymmetry and longitudinal channel-profile breaks across multiple neighboring catchments; require repeated orientation-consistent anomalies across independent valleys rather than a single scarp or knickpoint.
hypotheses.why_it_may_find_catalogue_missing_faults: Blind or low-relief displacement can tilt drainage networks, produce aligned channel deflections, or create repeated profile breaks where no continuous Quaternary surface trace is mapped. A multi-catchment rule could distinguish a regional structural signal from one local landform.
hypotheses.difference_from_repository_prior_art: This repeated drainage-response test is not the existing maximum LiDAR scarp-line integral, pixel classifier, or catalogue-tip bridge. The cached DEM is only 100 m aggregated, so it cannot support the intended 1 m channel/profile signature; using it alone would change and weaken the hypothesis.
hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Lithologic knickpoints, stream capture, fan-head incision, terrace risers, roads, and irrigation channels can produce profile asymmetry or channel deflection.
hypotheses.qualitative_expected_improvement: Rank 3; potentially useful scale-specific evidence, but expected value is unquantified and presently blocked by raw-data availability.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: High: obtain and hash raw tiles, verify CRS/coverage/licence, derive hydrologic profiles, control for lithology and land-use artifacts, then run spatially blocked tests.

shared_validation_requirements.evaluator: Reuse the repository's shared hide-and-recover evaluator and writer; do not maintain a private fork.
shared_validation_requirements.split: Withhold whole fault segments with a spatial buffer; derive every catalogue-based feature from fold-visible faults only; mask visible faults pixel-exactly.
shared_validation_requirements.metric: Pooled DTI with alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, and the 300 m triangular kernel; report evaluator version, withheld-positive count, and 95% CI.
shared_validation_requirements.leakage: Test every feature alone; AUC > 0.90 is leakage until proven otherwise.
shared_validation_requirements.uniqueness: Check the continuous surface before placement and final dots; stop if rank-correlation exceeds 0.90 or more than 70% of dots fall within 3 px of any registry raster.
shared_validation_requirements.promotion: Require a fresh screen, an independent frozen confirmation, passing leakage and both uniqueness checks, saved-byte format validation, and a separate fail-closed selector. Do not upload or choose a weekly slot in this workstream.
